[[COVID-19 anti-lockdown protests in New Zealand|Anti-lockdown]]}} | headquarters = | website = https://freedom.kiwi/ | international = }} The '''New Zealand Outdoors & Freedom Party,''' formerly known as the New Zealand Outdoors Party, is a registered [[political party]] in [[New Zealand]]. The party is led by [[Sue Grey (lawyer)|Sue Grey]]. The party's policies combine environmentalism with anti-government conspiracy theories.{{cite web |url=http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO1509/S00269/a-new-political-party-based-on-the-outdoors.htm |title=A new political party based on the Outdoors.. |publisher=Scoop |date=21 September 2015 |access-date=21 September 2015}}{{cite news |last1=Manch |first1=Thomas |title='Shocked' Outdoors and Freedom Party has not agreed to political alliance with Brian Tamaki |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/129669888/shocked-outdoors-and-freedom-party-has-not-agreed-to-political-alliance-with-brian-tamaki |access-date=16 May 2023 |publisher=Stuff |date=24 August 2022 |quote=The Outdoors and Freedom Party and its co-leader, Sue Grey, have been heavily involved in the anti-Covid-19 vaccine and mandate movement, have spread conspiracy theories about the efficacy of the vaccine, and participated in an occupation of Parliament grounds earlier in the year, which ended with a destructive riot.}} A minor party, it has never had a member of Parliament. ==Principles and policies== The Freedom Party's policy platform includes opposition to fluoridation of water,{{cite web |last1=Simmons |first1=Alan |title=Flurode in Water |url=https://outdoorsparty.co.nz/flouride-in-water/ |website=Outdoors & Freedom Party |access-date=16 May 2023 |date=6 May 2023}} [[1080 poison]], vaccines, COVID-19 restrictions, and [[5G]] technology.{{cite web |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/118766366/lawyer-sue-grey-aims-to-win-nelson-electorate-seat-for-nz-outdoors-party |title=Lawyer Sue Grey aims to win Nelson electorate seat for NZ Outdoors Party |publisher=Stuff |author=Cherie Sivignon |date=14 January 2020 |access-date=27 August 2020 |quote=Among its policies, the NZ Outdoors Party calls for the immediate cessation and use of 1080 poison, supports the use of medicinal cannabis and seeks a moratorium on the allocation, auction and rollout of 5G spectrum licences until there has been a full public inquiry into the costs and benefits of 5G, effects on human health and the natural environment and how these can best be avoided or managed.}} They support [[medicinal cannabis]]. These newer policy positions have been added to the party's original platform, which aims to protect the environment and New Zealand's "outdoors heritage". At its launch the party advocated for clean, full and unmodified rivers, greater protection from development for the conservation estate, large game animals to be managed by all hunters for recreation and conservation benefit, removal of ecologically destructive trawling practices within the inshore fishery and a Futures Commission to determine environmental limits to the growth of population, tourism, economy and infrastructure.{{cite news |url=http://www.newshub.co.nz/home/election/2017/08/the-outdoors-party-wants-to-get-into-parliament.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170822100546/http://www.newshub.co.nz/home/election/2017/08/the-outdoors-party-wants-to-get-into-parliament.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=22 August 2017 |title=The Outdoors Party wants to get into Parliament |newspaper=[[Newshub]] |date=22 August 2017 |access-date=22 August 2017}} ==History== === Creation and 2017 election === The New Zealand Outdoors Party was launched in September 2015 by co-leaders Alan Simmons, formerly of the [[United Future]] party, and David Haynes, president of the Association of Freshwater Anglers.{{cite news |last1=Anderson |first1=Charles |title=Outdoors Party New Zealand founder hopes general election a watershed moment |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/91036051/outdoors-party-new-zealand-founder-hopes-general-election-a-watershed-moment |access-date=21 May 2023 |publisher=Stuff |date=30 March 2017}} The new party aimed to protect New Zealand's environment and outdoor heritage. After building up its membership over the next two years,{{Cite web|url=http://www.outdoorsparty.co.nz/newsletters/december2016.htm|title=NZ Outdoors Party Newsletter December 2016|website=www.outdoorsparty.co.nz|access-date=2017-01-22}}{{Cite web|url=http://www.outdoorsparty.co.nz/newsletters/september2016.htm|title=NZ Outdoors Party Newsletter|website=www.outdoorsparty.co.nz|access-date=2017-01-22}} the party was granted registration by the Electoral Commission on 11 August 2017.{{cite web |url=http://www.elections.org.nz/news-media/application-register-political-party-and-logo-0 |title=Application to register political party and logo |publisher=Electoral Commission |date=22 July 2017 |access-date=28 July 2017}}{{cite web |url=http://www.elections.org.nz/news-media/registration-nz-outdoors-party-and-logo |title=Registration of NZ Outdoors Party and Logo |publisher=Electoral Commission |date=11 August 2017 |access-date=11 August 2017}} In the [[New Zealand general election, 2017|2017 general election]] the party stood candidates in [[Nelson (New Zealand electorate)|Nelson]], [[Taupō (New Zealand electorate)|Taupō]], [[Maungakiekie (New Zealand electorate)|Maungakiekie]] and [[Hutt South (New Zealand electorate)|Hutt South]]. The same four were also on the party list. With 0.1% of the party vote the Outdoors Party failed to win any seats in the [[New Zealand House of Representatives]].{{cite web|title=2017 General Election - Official Result|url=http://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2017/|publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|New Zealand Electoral Commission]]|access-date=7 October 2017}} === 2020: Pandemic response, protests, and election === ====Relationships with other minor parties==== Following the de-registration of the [[Ban 1080 Party]] in 2017, many Ban 1080 supporters moved to the Outdoors Party. In January 2020 it was announced that the party elected anti-1080 activist Sue Grey as its co-leader.{{cite news |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2020/01/outdoors-party-reckons-it-can-ride-an-anti-1080-wave-to-parliament-in-2020.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200121111656/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2020/01/outdoors-party-reckons-it-can-ride-an-anti-1080-wave-to-parliament-in-2020.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=21 January 2020 |title=Outdoors Party reckons it can ride an anti-1080 wave to Parliament in 2020 |newspaper=[[Newshub]] |date=12 January 2020 |access-date=27 August 2020}} Co-founder David Haynes left the party around the same time.{{cite news |last1=Johnston |first1=Kirsty |title=Just asking questions: How lawyer Sue Grey became the hero of New Zealand's conspiracy underbelly |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/health/coronavirus/128296235/just-asking-questions-how-lawyer-sue-grey-became-the-hero-of-new-zealands-conspiracy-underbelly |access-date=21 May 2023 |publisher=Stuff |date=13 December 2022 |quote=After Grey joined - and Haynes departed - its policies expanded, calling for the immediate cessation of the use of 1080, a moratorium on the allocation of medicinal marijuana, and an inquiry into 5G.}} In March 2020 the party formed an alliance with the Real NZ Party, resulting in the founder and leader of Real NZ, [[David Moffett]], being appointed to the Outdoor Party's board as an executive director. Jennie Brown, an early childhood educator from [[Gisborne, New Zealand|Gisborne]], was made a new board member at the same time.{{cite web |url=https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO2003/S00246/former-rugby-ceo-david-moffett-joins-the-nz-outdoors-party-as-executive-director.htm?from-mobile=bottom-link-01 |title=Former Rugby CEO David Moffett Joins The NZ Outdoors Party As Executive Director |publisher=Scoop |date=23 March 2020 |access-date=8 April 2020}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.outdoorsparty.co.nz/march-2020-newsletter/|title=March 2020 Newsletter|website=NZ Outdoors Party|date=April 2020 }} By the time of the election, Brown was standing as a candidate for the [[Billy Te Kahika]]'s [[New Zealand Public Party]] (NZPP).{{cite web |title=Let the election games begin |url=https://www.gisborneherald.co.nz/local-news/20200721/let-the-election-games-begin/ |publisher=Gisborne Herald |access-date=21 May 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210805184327/https://www.gisborneherald.co.nz/local-news/20200721/let-the-election-games-begin/ |archive-date=5 August 2021|date=21 July 2020}} In April 2020 the NZPP, known for its belief in a "plandemic" conspiracy, had approached the Outdoors Party about working together but a personality clash between Te Kahika and Sue Grey prevented this.{{cite news |last1=Daalder |first1=Marc |title=Jami-Lee Ross hitches wagon to conspiracy theorists |url=https://www.newsroom.co.nz/jami-lee-ross-hitches-wagon-to-conspiracy-theorists |access-date=15 May 2023 |publisher=Newsroom |date=July 26, 2020 |quote=A prospective union with the Outdoors Party fell apart due to personality clashes between Te Kahika and anti-1080 lawyer and Outdoors candidate Sue Grey, according to posts from the NZPP Facebook page.}} Within four months the relationship reached a point where Grey alleged that the Outdoors Party had been the target of a harassment campaign by NZPP supporters (which was now in allied with [[Advance New Zealand]]). Te Kahika called the behaviour "absolutely reprehensible" and asked his supporters not to abuse Grey, but also said that “the worst and the filthiest behaviour has actually come from Outdoors Party supporters towards the Public Party".{{cite web |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/122289676/fringe-party-leader-alleges-campaign-of-harassment-by-billy-tk-supporters |title=Fringe party leader alleges campaign of harassment by Billy TK supporters |author=Andrea Vance |work=[[Stuff (website)|Stuff]] |date=1 August 2020 |access-date=27 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200806215602/https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/122289676/fringe-party-leader-alleges-campaign-of-harassment-by-billy-tk-supporters|archive-date=6 August 2020|url-status=live}} ====Protests, split, and election==== In April 2020 the party criticised a nationwide lockdown (a response to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand|COVID-19 pandemic]]) as "cruel and unreasonable" as it banned hunting and other outdoor activities. They also compared the New Zealand Government to the [[Nazi Party]].{{cite web |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=12322620 |title=Covid 19 coronavirus: NZ Outdoors Party criticises lockdown rules |publisher=New Zealand Herald |date=5 April 2020 |access-date=27 August 2020}} In June 2020, at a rally in [[Auckland]], Outdoors Party supporters claimed that the [[September 11 attacks]] were a [[false flag]] operation, promoted [[flat Earth]] theories, and denounced "mind control" and 5G technology.{{cite web |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/300070891/the-conspiracists-election-how-the-farthest-fringes-of-politics-are-making-a-play-for-the-centre |title=The conspiracists' election: How the farthest fringes of politics are making a play for the centre |author=Charlie Mitchell |publisher=Stuff |date=1 August 2020 |access-date=27 August 2020}} They also harassed and threatened a young Asian woman who wiped out chalk slogans saying "[[it's okay to be white]]" and "[[all lives matter]]". One supporter screamed at the woman to “go back to her own country”, while another said "she wasn't born here, she came here to create shit". Party co-leader Alan Simmons reprimanded the woman, saying "you shouldn't be using language like that, a little girl like you". Party member Tracy Livingston tried to ease tension, saying that the young woman was "not the enemy" and that everybody was "naturally racist". Party co-leader Sue Grey later told media that the people in the video were not members of the party, that the party did not condone their actions, and that two of the people in the incident had since apologised to her. Simmons also spoke to media afterwards, saying he had "protected the girl" from harm.{{cite web|url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/news/article.cfm?c_id=1&objectid=12338855|title=Watch: Woman told 'go back to your own country' for wiping out 'it's okay to be white' chalk|publisher=The New Zealand Herald|date=11 June 2020}} Around September 2020, at least six nominated candidates pulled out of the party. Some switched allegiance to the [[New Zealand Public Party]] or the [[Social Credit Party (New Zealand)|Social Credit Party]] while others founded a new party called the Attica Project.{{cite web|author=Braae|first=Alex|date=18 September 2020|title=Candidates defect in all directions in ugly minor party battle|url=https://thespinoff.co.nz/politics/18-09-2020/candidates-defect-in-all-directions-in-ugly-minor-party-battle/|access-date=18 September 2020|publisher=The Spinoff}} The New Zealand Outdoors Party received a broadcasting allocation of $51,821 for the [[2020 New Zealand general election|2020 election]].{{cite web |url=https://elections.nz/media-and-news/2020/2020-broadcasting-allocation-decision-released/ |title=2020 Broadcasting Allocation Decision Released |publisher=Electoral Commission |date=29 May 2020 |access-date=29 May 2020}} It received 3,256 party votes, or 0.1% of the total.{{cite web|title=2020 General Election and Referendums - Official Result|url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2020/|publisher=New Zealand Electoral Commission}} ===2022: NZ Outdoors & Freedom Party, Freedoms NZ, and by-elections=== {{Main|Freedoms NZ}} In April 2022 the party officially changed its name to the NZ Outdoors & Freedom Party.{{cite web |url=https://elections.nz/media-and-news/2022/change-to-nz-outdoors-and-freedom-party-name-and-logo/ |title=Change to NZ Outdoors & Freedom Party name and logo |publisher=New Zealand Electoral Commission |date=7 April 2022 |access-date=18 June 2022}} The next month [[Donna Pokere-Phillips]] became co-leader in place of Simmons, a position she held until 2025. Pokere-Phillips had previously stood in elections for the [[Māori Party]] (Te Pāti Māori, 2020), [[The Opportunities Party]] (TOP, 2017), and the [[Alliance (New Zealand political party)|Alliance]] (1999).{{cite web |title=Percentage of Electorate Candidate Votes of successful registered parties |url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_1999/e9/html/e9_partVII.html |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |accessdate=26 July 2020}}{{cite press release |title=TOP Announces Party List for 2017 General Election |url=http://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO1708/S00554/top-announces-party-list-for-2017-general-election.htm |publisher=The Opportunities Party |agency=[[Scoop (website)|Scoop]] |date=28 August 2017 |accessdate=28 August 2017}}{{cite news |title=Maori Party new opportunity for Pokere-Phillips |url=https://www.waateanews.com/waateanews/x_news/MjQzNTk/Paakiwaha/Maori-Party-new-opportunity-for-Pokere-Phillips |accessdate=26 July 2020 |work=Waatea News |date=4 May 2020}}{{cite web |title=New Co-Leader For Outdoors & Freedom Party |url=https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO2205/S00069/new-co-leader-for-outdoors-freedom-party.htm |website=Scoop |publisher=NZ Outdoors and Freedom Party |access-date=26 July 2022 |date=9 May 2022}} Sue Grey stood as the party's candidate in the [[2022 Tauranga by-election]], held on 18 June. She received 1,030 votes, the fourth-highest total out of 20,784 cast. (Winning candidate [[Sam Uffindell]] received 11,613.){{cite web |title=Tauranga by-election official results |url=https://elections.nz/media-and-news/2022/tauranga-by-election-official-results/ |website=Electoral Commission |access-date=21 May 2023 |date=1 July 2022}} On 23 August 2022 [[The Freedoms & Rights Coalition]], led by [[Brian Tamaki]], held a protest outside Parliament. Tamaki announced that a new umbrella party, [[Freedoms NZ]], would be formed through a union of the Outdoors & Freedom Party, [[Vision NZ]] (led by his wife [[Hannah Tamaki|Hannah]]), and the nascent [[New Nation Party]]. He also invited other minor parties to join.{{cite news |last1=Witton |first1=Bridie |title=Brian Tamaki brings fringe political parties into new group Freedoms NZ |access-date=24 August 2022 |publisher=Stuff |date=23 August 2022| url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/politics/129657797/brian-tamaki-brings-fringe-political-parties-into-new-group-freedoms-nz}} The Outdoors & Freedom Party responded that Tamaki's announcement was premature, and that they had not decided whether to join Freedoms NZ.{{cite web |title=Tamaki's new Freedoms coalition hits a bump in the road (Live Update) |url=https://thespinoff.co.nz/live-updates/24-08-2022/tamakis-new-freedoms-coalition-hits-a-bump-in-the-road |website=The Spinoff |access-date=24 August 2022 |date=24 August 2022|first=Stewart |last=Sowman-Lund}}{{cite news |title=Parliament protest: Brian Tamaki announces new umbrella political party 'Freedoms NZ' |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/parliament-protest-brian-tamaki-announces-new-umbrella-political-party-freedoms-nz/GYZSQDORMUKGO7MP3OMMAN2D6Q/ |access-date=23 August 2022 |publisher=New Zealand Herald |date=23 August 2022}} The first parliamentary election held after the formation of Freedoms NZ was the [[2022 Hamilton West by-election]]. Vision NZ and Outdoors & Freedom entered separate candidates (Freedoms NZ was not a registered party at the time).{{cite web |title=Vision NZ announces candidate for Hamilton West |url=http://www.voxy.co.nz/politics/5/409467 |website=Voxy |access-date=8 November 2022 |date=8 November 2022}} Donna Pokere-Phillips, the Outdoors & Freedom co-leader, received 125 votes, less than 1% of the total.{{cite web |title=Hamilton West - Preliminary Count |url=https://www.electionresults.govt.nz/2022_hamilton_west_byelection_preliminary/ |website=Election Results |publisher=Electoral Commission New Zealand |access-date=15 December 2022}} ====2022 local elections==== A number of candidates in the [[2022 New Zealand local elections]] were affiliated with the Outdoors & Freedom Party: * Co-leader Donna Pokere-Phillips placed fourth in [[2022 Hamilton, New Zealand mayoral election|Hamilton's mayoral election]] and third in the [[Hamilton City Council (New Zealand)|city council]]'s new Maaori Ward, which elected only two members.{{cite news |last1=Franke-Bowell |first1=Jonah |title=One candidate, two parties: Conservative coalition picks Hamilton West contender |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/waikato-times/news/300732811/one-candidate-two-parties-conservative-coalition-picks-hamilton-west-contender |access-date=7 November 2022 |publisher=Stuff |date=7 November 2022|quote=Donna Pokere-Phillips will contest the by-election for the NZ Outdoors and Freedom Party. }}{{cite web |title=Result: LGE 2022 - Final |url=https://www.yourcityelections.co.nz/assets/Uploads/Results-page/Hamilton-City-Council-Final-results-for-the-2022-Election.pdf |website=Your City Elections |access-date=8 November 2022 |date=14 October 2022 |archive-date=16 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221016053954/https://www.yourcityelections.co.nz/assets/Uploads/Results-page/Hamilton-City-Council-Final-results-for-the-2022-Election.pdf |url-status=dead }} * Party board member Aly Cook also placed fourth in her bid to be mayor of the [[Tasman District Council]].{{cite web |title=Previous election results |url=https://www.tasman.govt.nz/my-council/about-us/your-mayor-and-councillors/local-elections/election-results/ |website=Tasman District Council |access-date=24 May 2023}} While campaigning she said she shared values with anti-vaccination group [[Voices for Freedom]]. She also falsely claimed that the Government report, [[He Puapua]], has come from the [[United Nations]] and that [[COVID-19 vaccine misinformation and hesitancy|COVID-19 vaccines contained nanotechnology]].{{cite news |last1=Ridout |first1=Amy |last2=Chin |first2=Frances |last3=Sivignon |first3=Cherie |title=Former principal and current councillor among seven Tasman candidates with links to conspiracies and disinformation |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/129640451/former-principal-and-current-councillor-among-seven-tasman-candidates-with-links-to-conspiracies-and-disinformation |access-date=24 May 2023 |publisher=Stuff |date=31 August 2022}}{{cite news |last1=Sivignon |first1=Cherie |title=TDC mayoral race: Aly Cook keen for council to help repair social cohesion |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/nelson-mail/nelson-top-stories/129856965/tdc-mayoral-race-aly-cook-keen-for-council-to-help-repair-social-cohesion |access-date=24 May 2023 |publisher=Stuff |date=21 September 2022}} * Hine Afeaki finished fourth in [[Auckland Council|Auckland]]'s Manukau Ward, which elected two councillors.{{cite web |title=Ward councillor official results (2022) |url=https://www.aucklandcouncil.govt.nz/elections/elections-2022-results/Pages/results-ward-councillors.aspx |website=Vote Auckland |publisher=Auckland Council |access-date=24 May 2023}} She was also an unsuccessful tenth in the Māngere-Ōtāhuhu Local Board election.{{cite web |title=Local board member official results |url=https://www.aucklandcouncil.govt.nz/elections/elections-2022-results/Pages/results-local-board-members.aspx |website=Vote Auckland |publisher=Auckland Council |access-date=24 May 2023}} ===2023–25: General election and Freedoms NZ=== Changing its earlier position, the Outdoors & Freedom Party joined [[Freedoms New Zealand|Freedoms NZ]] in May 2023. Sue Grey and Brian Tamaki were announced as co-leaders of the umbrella movement.{{cite news |title=Outdoors Party reveals it's joining forces with Brian Tamaki's Freedoms NZ |url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2023/05/outdoors-party-reveals-it-s-joining-forces-with-brian-tamaki-s-freedoms-nz.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230513020620/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/politics/2023/05/outdoors-party-reveals-it-s-joining-forces-with-brian-tamaki-s-freedoms-nz.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=13 May 2023 |access-date=14 May 2023 |publisher=[[Newshub]] |date=13 May 2023}}{{cite news |title=Brian Tamaki to run for Parliament as Freedom NZ leader |url=https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/national/489821/brian-tamaki-to-run-for-parliament-as-freedom-nz-leader |access-date=14 May 2023 |publisher=[[RNZ]] |date=13 May 2023}}{{cite news |title=Brian Tamaki vs Newshub: TV show pulls Destiny Church leader interview off-air |access-date=14 May 2023 |publisher=New Zealand Herald |date=13 May 2023|url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/brian-tamaki-vs-newshub-tv-show-pulls-destiny-church-leader-interview-off-air-at-last-moment/FIV3R6V2OBDDBH7OQJXGYLYP7E/}} Parties that gained less than 1% of 2020's party vote are eligible for $66,332 in broadcast funding from the Electoral Commission. Before Outdoors & Freedom joined Freedoms NZ, the commission had signalled that this amount would be allocated to the party. Once the party joined Freedoms NZ the Commission said it was likely that Freedoms NZ would be treated as a single "group of parties" eligible for only one allocation of $66,332. Constituent parties, including Outdoors & Freedom, would not receive individual allocations. Sue Grey and Brian Tamaki began challenging the Electoral Commission in the High Court on May 31, arguing that there was no formal relationship between Freedoms NZ and Outdoors & Freedom.{{cite news |last1=Griffiths |first1=Ethan |title=Sue Grey and Brian Tamaki launch High Court action over election campaign funding |url=https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/sue-grey-and-brian-tamaki-launch-high-court-action-over-election-campaign-funding/LNEGKH6G7FDNNEGI37ZPS65T3M/ |access-date=31 May 2023 |publisher=New Zealand Herald |date=31 May 2023}} The New Zealand High Court dismissed the plaintiffs' claims.{{Cite web |last=The High Court of New Zealand |date=17 July 2023 |title=New Zealand Outdoors and Freedom Party v the Electoral Commission [2023] NZHC 1823 |url=https://www.courtsofnz.govt.nz/assets/cases/2023/MR-2023-NZHC-1823.pdf }}{{Dead link|date=September 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} A few days later, Sue Grey said that her party would "review" claims made by [[Counterspin Media|Counterspin]], a far-right media platform with strong links to the broader "freedom" movement and a history of airing conspiracy theories, in a video that attacked Brian and Hannah Tamaki for profiting as the landlords of a Covid testing site. Amidst other simultaneous signals of disunity between anti-mandate groups, Grey also suggested that there would be room under the Freedoms NZ umbrella for more parties.{{cite news |last1=Roberts |first1=Nadine |title=Freedom movement splintering amid infighting and the formation of new political party |url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/national/132238189/freedom-movement-splintering-amid-infighting-and-the-formation-of-new-political-party |access-date=7 June 2023 |publisher=Stuff |date=7 June 2023}} Final results from the [[2023 New Zealand general election]] indicate that Freedoms New Zealand received 0.33% (9,586 votes) of the party vote and did not win any electorate seats, meaning it did not enter parliament. Sue Grey came seventh of nine in the [[West Coast-Tasman]] electorate.{{cite web |title=2023 General Election - Official Result |url=https://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/ |publisher=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] |access-date=11 December 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231205020139/https://archive.electionresults.govt.nz/electionresults_2023/ |archive-date=5 December 2023 |date=3 November 2023 |url-status=live}} In May 2025, Freedoms NZ was deregistered as a party and disbanded as an umbrella movement. The Outdoors and Freedom Party continues as its own entity.{{cite web |title=Public Announcement: Freedoms NZ to Deregister |url=https://www.freedomsnz.org.nz/ |website=Freedoms NZ |access-date=3 June 2025 |quote=[Component] parties now have their own goals and direction...and we wish them every success."}} After its 2025 AGM, the party announced that "Sue Grey continues as Leader", with no mention of Pokere-Phillips.{{cite web |last1=NZ Outdoors and Freedom Party |title=Outdoors & Freedom Party AGM |url=https://www.scoop.co.nz/stories/PO2508/S00183/outdoors-freedom-party-agm.htm |website=Scoop |access-date=13 October 2025 |date=31 August 2025}} The party listed her tenure as co-leader as ending in 2025.{{Cite web |title=Wise Council Members |url=https://freedom.kiwi/wise-council |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260720202640/https://freedom.kiwi/wise-council |archive-date=20 July 2026 |access-date=11 September 2026 |website=NZ Outdoors & Freedom Party}} In July 2026, the party applied to change their name to "Freedom" and amend their party logo.{{Cite web |title=Application to change party name and logo |url=https://elections.nz/media-and-news/2026/application-to-change-party-name-and-logo |access-date=5 August 2026 |website=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]}} In August, the [[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]] declined the application.{{cite web |url=https://elections.nz/media-and-news/2026/decisions-on-party-registrations-and-logos|title=Decisions on party registrations and logos|date=5 August 2026|access-date=5 August 2026|website=[[Electoral Commission (New Zealand)|Electoral Commission]]}} == List of leaders == {| class="wikitable" |+ !No. !Name !Portrait !
